messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT firing: gpu-ecc-spike (gpu-node-12, region-us-west) - metric gpu.ecc.errors count > 5 in 5m. https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/GPUs/gpu-health?orgId=1&var-node=gpu-node-12

jordan (oncall): seeing the page. pulling up logs. anyone seeing customer 5xx spikes?

mira (sre): yes, noticed increased 503s to /generate for a handful of requests starting ~5m before alert. correlates with that host in the trace.

kai (runtime): node 12 reports repeated ECC corrected errors on GPU0 and GPU1, driver still up. I’m checking temperature/thermal throttles and recent OOMs.

selena (observability): dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood/d/GPUs/gpu-health?view=live - VRAM usage, ECC count, thermal_celsius. Panel shows VRAM on gpu0 at 92% for last 10m.

dima (engineer): quick check: we had a batch job pinned to that node earlier, might be causing sustained high VRAM. I can try to reschedule.

jordan (oncall): ok plan: 1) reduce immediate customer impact 2) isolate problematic node 3) quiet noisy alerts while we assess. I’ll page runtime for node drain.

kai (runtime): starting cordon/drain in a few. will `kubectl cordon gpu-node-12` then try to safely evict pods. If eviction blocks, we’ll do `--force` as last resort.

mira (sre): customers affected list from logs: 3 teams had elevated latencies (ingest, webapp-search, embeddings-service). Opening INC-487 to track.

jordan (oncall): command logs:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-12
kubectl drain gpu-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
```

kai (runtime): drain proceeding, one pod stuck in Terminating due to a local CSI mount. I’ll restart kubelet if it blocks.

selena (observability): noisy-ness note: ECC alert fires on any >0 corrected errors historically which floods pages during heavy batch runs. We should require either >5 errors in 5m AND VRAM >85% OR a driver error flag. Proposal in chat below.

dima (engineer): I can throttle the batch or migrate it off cluster in 10m if drain is still ongoing.

jordan (oncall): short mitigation: mute gpu-ecc-spike for 15m to avoid re-page while we drain. Will set an alert suppression. If errors continue after drain, we unmute and escalate.

selena (observability): creating a temporary silence: `alertmanager silence add --match alertname=gpu-ecc-spike --duration=15m --created-by=jordan`

mira (sre): +1 to temporary silence. But we need to update the rule post-incident to reduce false positives. Suggested rule:
```
- alert: gpu_ecc_spike
  expr: increase(gpu_ecc_errors_total[5m]) > 5 and avg_over_time(gpu_memory_used_bytes[5m]) / gpu_memory_total_bytes > 0.85
  for: 2m
  labels:
    severity: page
```

kai (runtime): drain finished, node cordoned and pods evicted. `kubectl uncordon` not run obviously. GPU driver shows corrected errors dropping after eviction. No current customer-facing errors.

jordan (oncall): thanks. Jordan -> on-call summary: node isolated, batch job migrated by dima, temp silence active. Customers show degraded latency for ~8m window, now recovering.

selena (observability): follow-up dashboard work: add an 'ECC trend by GPU' panel and composite alert that combines ECC spikes + VRAM pressure + driver resets. I’ll open OBS-312 for the dashboard and link to INC-487.

mira (sre): post-incident tasks: 1) update runbook section for GPU ECC (add thresholds & actions) 2) tune alert (as selena suggested) 3) add playbook step for safe drain including CSI mount fallback 4) schedule retro. I’ll own the runbook update.

dima (engineer): note: application should handle transient corrected ECC errors - we should confirm no data corruption. I’ll run model checksum tests for the affected model after node is back.

jordan (oncall): handing off to mira for longer term work — I’m off in ~30m. Mira, can you pick up follow-ups and coordinate with runtime/observability?

mira (sre): taking it. I’ll create the follow-up ticket list and set a 1h postmortem sync for the incident.

selena (observability): action items I’ll create: OBS-312 (dashboard + composite alert), OBS-313 (alert rule change PR), and temp alert mute notes in INC-487.

kai (runtime): will run a healthcheck on the node after we uncordon and watch ECC counts for 24h. If we see repeated corrected errors + thermals > 85C we schedule hardware review.

dima (engineer): tests queued. I’ll post results in INC-487.

jordan (oncall): thanks team. final note: we changed the alerting logic immediate triage to require VRAM >85% with >5 ECC in 5m and a 2m for clause — reduces noise from occasional single bit corrections. Also added dashboard and runbook items. I’m marking my handoff in rotation tool. :thumbsup:

mira (sre): acknowledged. I’ll post the incident summary and assign owners. 1h postmortem invite to the group.

incident-bot: Incident INC-487 created by mira. Postmortem meeting scheduled at 2025-03-28T16:00:00Z.

jordan (oncall): off shift, thanks all.

mira (sre): closing thread for now, will update with ticket links and PRs.
